issues.description:
Element: Animal.messageOnFeed()
Problem statement / UML: The UML in problem_statement.md declares messageOnFeed() with a leading '+' (public) and shows it as an abstract method ("+ messageOnFeed():String") indicating the method should be public and abstract.
Solution repository: solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java declares the method as protected abstract ("protected abstract String messageOnFeed();").
Impact: This visibility mismatch leaves students unsure whether they must declare messageOnFeed() as public or protected. It can be confusing when writing subclasses and when other classes (e.g., Farm) invoke the method; instructors/tests may expect the visibility from the UML (public) while the reference solution uses protected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent between the specification and the reference solution. Preferred fix: change the solution method declaration to public to match the UML, e.g. in Animal.java use: public abstract String messageOnFeed(); and keep subclasses overriding it as public. Alternative: if the intended design is to restrict visibility, update the UML and problem text to show messageOnFeed() as protected so students follow the narrower visibility.
